He previously played for the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]]. ==Early life and high school career== Johnson grew up in [[Norfolk, Virginia]] and originally attended [[Norview High School]] before transferring to [[IMG Academy]] in [[Bradenton, Florida]] before his junior year.{{cite web|url=https://www.pilotonline.com/757teamz/basketball/article_5545f923-f863-5ee3-8773-2f9fc606b48e.html|title=Former Norview star makes impressive return to South Hampton Roads|first1=Larry|last1=Rubama|first2=Brian|last2=Saunders|work=[[The Virginian-Pilot]]|date=January 30, 2017|access-date=March 13, 2020}} He played at IMG for one season before transferring again to [[Oak Hill Academy (Mouth of Wilson, Virginia)|Oak Hill Academy]] in [[Mouth of Wilson, Virginia]] for his senior season after his head coach, Vince Walden, left the school to become an assistant coach at [[Arkansas State Red Wolves men's basketball|Arkansas State]]. During the [[Nike Elite Youth Basketball League|Nike EYBL]] finals at Peach Jam, Johnson averaged 12.9 points and 7.6 rebounds per game.{{cite web|url=https://www.slamonline.com/college-hs/keyontae-johnson/|title=Florida Commit Keyontae Johnson is Ready for the Big Stage|first=Brett|last=Regan|work=[[Slam (magazine)|Slam]]|date=January 24, 2018|access-date=March 13, 2020}} As a senior, he scored at least 18 points in 19 of Oak Hill's games.{{cite web|url=https://gatorswire.usatoday.com/2020/01/16/mens-basketball-profile-keyontae-johnson/|title=Men's basketball profile: Keyontae Johnson|first=Ted|last=Rydquist|website=Gators Wire|publisher=[[USA Today]]|date=January 16, 2020|access-date=March 13, 2020}} Rated a four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] by [[247Sports]] and [[ESPN]] (who also rated him as a top 100 recruit), Johnson committed to playing college basketball for [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] over an offer from [[Texas Tech Red Raiders basketball|Texas Tech]] while also receiving interest from [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]], [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]], [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]], [[Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball|Wake Forest]] and [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]].{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2722871-4-star-sf-prospect-keyontae-johnson-commits-to-florida-over-texas-tech|title=4-Star SF Prospect Keyontae Johnson Commits to Florida over Texas Tech|first=Scott|last=Polacek|website=[[Bleacher Report]]|date=November 10, 2017|access-date=March 13, 2020}}{{cite web|url=http://www.startribune.com/four-star-wing-keyontae-johnson-would-bring-versatility-and-athleticism-to-gophers/450789173/|title=Four-star wing Keyontae Johnson would bring versatility and athleticism to Gophers|work=[[Star Tribune]]|date=October 13, 2017|access-date=March 13, 2020}}{{cite web|url=http://www.wruf.com/headlines/2019/10/14/keyontae-johnson-an-emerging-leader-with-a-new-attitude/|title=Keyontae Johnson: An Emerging Leader with a New Attitude|first=Camille|last=Woodhouse|website=WRUF.com|date=October 14, 2019|access-date=March 13, 2020}} ==College career== ===Florida=== In 2018, Johnson began his true freshman season as a key [[substitution (sport)|reserve]], and eventually became the Gators' starting [[small forward]] going into the team's game against [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]]. He started the final 20 games of the season, and finished the season with 8.1 points, 6.4 rebounds, and 1.3 assists per game.{{cite web|url=https://247sports.com/LongFormArticle/college-basketball-best-small-forward-rankings-Jordan-Nwora-132873716/|title=The best small forwards in college basketball for 2019-20|first=Kevin|last=Flaherty|website=247Sports.com|date=June 14, 2019|access-date=March 13, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/florida/basketball/florida-gators-keyontae-johnson-depended-on-auburn-baylor|title=Keyontae Johnson Will Be Depended On Entering Gators' Tough Stretch|first=Brandon|last=Carroll|website=[[Sports Illustrated|SI.com]]|date=January 18, 2020|access-date=March 13, 2020}} Johnson averaged 13.7 points and 10 rebounds during the [[2019 SEC men's basketball tournament]], as the Gators went to the tournament semifinal. He scored 20 points and 12 rebounds in the opening round against [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]], a [[double-double]].{{cite web|url=https://www.collegesportsmadness.com/article/17934|title=#10 FLORIDA MEN'S BASKETBALL 2019-2020 PREVIEW|first=Jacob|last=Young|website=CollegeSportsMadness.com|date=October 27, 2019|access-date=March 13, 2020}}{{cite web|url=http://www.wruf.com/headlines/2019/03/14/gators-open-up-sec-tournament-with-win-over-arkansas/|title=Gators Open Up SEC Tournament with Win Over Arkansas|first=Joey|last=Levy|website=WRUF.com|date=March 14, 2019|access-date=March 13, 2020}} On February 26, 2020, Johnson scored a career-high 25 points to go with 11 rebounds in an 81–66 win against [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]].{{cite news |title=Career nights for Johnson, Lewis as Florida thumps LSU 81-66 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166373 |date=February 26, 2020 |accessdate=March 23, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} As a sophomore, he averaged 14 points, 7.1 rebounds, 1.6 assists and 1.2 steals per game and was named first team All-[[Southeastern Conference|SEC]].{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/versatile-johnson-is-key-to-floridas-late-season-surge/2020/03/05/21e680be-5f22-11ea-ac50-18701e14e06d_story.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200306181749/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/versatile-johnson-is-key-to-floridas-late-season-surge/2020/03/05/21e680be-5f22-11ea-ac50-18701e14e06d_story.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=March 6, 2020|title=Versatile Johnson is 'Key' to Florida's late-season surge|first=Mark|last=Long|newspaper=[[The Washington Post]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|date=March 5, 2020|access-date=March 13, 2020}}{{cite web|url=https://www.news-press.com/story/sports/college/2020/03/11/florida-basketball-gators-keyontae-johnson-sec-tournament/5022849002/|title=Florida basketball: Keyontae Johnson ready to take over for Gators in SEC Tournament|first=Graham|last=Hall|work=[[The News-Press]]|publisher=[[The Gainesville Sun]]|date=March 11, 2020|access-date=March 13, 2020}} On December 12, 2020, Johnson collapsed on the court in a game at [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]].{{cite web |last1=Medcalf |first1=Myron |title=Florida Gators star Keyontae Johnson collapses on court |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/30502823/florida-gators-star-keyontae-johnson-collapses-court |website=ESPN |access-date=December 12, 2020 |date=December 12, 2020}} When he arrived at [[Tallahassee Memorial HealthCare|Tallahassee Memorial Hospital]], doctors assessed him to be in critical, but stable condition. After three days in a medically induced coma at Tallahassee Memorial, Johnson was taken back to [[Gainesville, Florida]] for further treatment. On December 15, it was reported that he was awake, speaking,{{Cite news|title=Florida basketball player Keyontae Johnson speaking, calling teammates via FaceTime {{!}} CBC Sports|language=en-US|work=CBC|url=https://www.cbc.ca/sports/basketball/keyontae-johnson-florida-basketball-update-1.5842768|access-date=2020-12-17}} and responding to commands.{{cite web |last1=Jackson |first1=Wilton |title=Florida's Keyontae Johnson Is in Critical, Stable Condition After On-Court Collapse |url=https://www.si.com/college/2020/12/12/florida-keyontae-johnson-collapses-vs-florida-state |website=Sports Illustrated |access-date=December 12, 2020 |date=December 12, 2020}} On December 28, head coach [[Mike White (basketball)|Mike White]] announced that Johnson had rejoined the team as a coach.{{Cite web |url=https://apnews.com/article/gainesville-florida-gators-mens-basketball-coronavirus-pandemic-mike-white-keyontae-johnson-29da567469d5e18d91c1d0a25f973916 |title=Florida's Johnson rejoins team, works as coach amid recovery |last=Long |first=Mark |date=December 28, 2020 |website=[[Associated Press]] |access-date=December 29, 2020}} Johnson was announced as the honorary starter on Senior Day against Kentucky on March 5, 2022, and received a standing ovation.{{Cite news |url=https://nypost.com/2022/03/06/floridas-keyontae-johnson-gets-ceremonial-start-after-2020-collapse/ |title=Keyontae Johnson gets ceremonial start for Florida 15 months after on-court collapse |newspaper=[[New York Post]] |date=2022-03-06 |access-date=2022-03-07}} On May 1, he entered the transfer portal.{{Cite web |title=Florida men's basketball player Keyontae Johnson enters name into NCAA transfer portal |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2022/05/01/keyontae-johnson-enters-transfer-portal-florida-gators/9611346002/ |access-date=May 1, 2022 |website=USA Today}} ===Kansas State=== On August 20, 2022, Johnson committed to Kansas State. Johnson was named [[Big 12 Conference|Big 12]] Newcomer of the Year and joined teammate [[Markquis Nowell]] on the First Team All-Big 12. Along with Nowell, Johnson led Kansas State to the Elite Eight in the 2023 NCAA Men's Basketball Tournament. {{cite news |last1=Gerber |first1=Lainey |title=Keyontae Johnson named Big 12 Newcomer of the Year |url=https://www.ksnt.com/sports/kansas-state-wildcats/keyontae-johnson-named-big-12-newcomer-of-the-year/ |access-date=March 6, 2023 |work=KSNT |date=March 5, 2023}} ==Pro career== On April 24, 2023, Johnson officially declared for the NBA Draft. With his heart issues, Johnson still needed to be cleared for contact by the NBA and did not participate in the physical components of the NBA Draft Combine. However, after being cleared by the NBA's Fitness to Play panel on May 26, 2023, Johnson officially kept his name in the NBA Draft and began working out for teams.{{Cite web |title=Keyontae Johnson declares for NBA Draft but leaves door open for Kansas State return |url=https://news.yahoo.com/keyontae-johnson-declares-nba-draft-130522740.html |access-date=June 6, 2023 |website=Yahoo}}{{Cite web |title=Keyontae Johnson cleared to be selected in NBA draft, agents say |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/37736729/keyontae-johnson-cleared-selected-nba-draft-agents-say/ |access-date=June 6, 2023 |website=ESPN}} ==Personal life== On March 16, 2022, [[Alachua County, Florida|Alachua County]] police filed a sworn complaint, claiming that Johnson sexually assaulted a woman, but the case was later dropped. Alachua County court records showed that prosecutors agreed to dismiss the case. {{Cite web |title=Florida basketball star Keyontae Johnson, who collapsed on court, accused of sexual battery |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/sec/2022/03/26/keyontae-johnson-accused-sexual-battery-florida-gators-basketball/7182330001/ |access-date=April 15, 2022 |website=USA Today}}{{Cite web |title=Florida basketball star Keyontae Johnson accused in sexual assault |url=https://www.wuft.org/news/2022/03/25/florida-basketball-star-keyontae-johnson-accused-in-sexual-assault/
